title: 3.7.8 Lab: Extract a Sub-List with `.slice()`
description: Create an array, copy a middle range and a run to the end with .slice(), then show the original is unchanged. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create the list
steps.instructions: Create a variable (the lesson calls it items; use any name that fits your list) and assign it an array of at least five values.

steps.title: Extract a middle range
steps.instructions: Use .slice(start, end) to copy a middle part of items into a new variable (the lesson calls it middle). Remember the end index is not included.

steps.title: Extract to the end
steps.instructions: Use .slice(start) with only a start index to copy everything from a position to the end of the array into another variable (the lesson calls it tail).

steps.title: Print the results and the original
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print both slices and the original items array, to confirm the original did not change.

requirements.title: Array declared
requirements.description: Declares an array with square brackets. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Declare an array (the lesson calls it items) with at least five values in square brackets.

requirements.title: Two .slice() calls
requirements.description: Calls .slice() at least twice. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Call .slice twice: once with a start and an end index, once with only a start. Keep each result in a variable.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Print both slices and the original items array.

requirements.title: items has five values and the slices and the original are printed
requirements.description: items has at least five values, middle is a part of it, tail runs from a start to the end of items, and the output shows both slices. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Make items a list of five or more values, take the two slices into their own variables, and print both slices and items.

checks.fail: items needs five or more values.
middle must take only PART of items: give .slice(start, end) a start and an end that leave some values out. A slice of everything is a copy, not a part.
tail must take only PART of items: give .slice(start) a start after 0, so it begins partway through.
tail should run to the END of items: use .slice(start) with only a start index, like items.slice(3).

checks.fail: Print both slices, middle and tail, so the output shows them.

requirements.title: middle and tail are sliced out of items and printed by code that runs
requirements.description: When items holds other values, middle and tail change with it, and console.log calls that run print both slices. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Make middle and tail with items.slice(...) and print each of them. A list typed in by hand, or typed-in output, does not change when items does.

checks.fail: middle has to be copied out of items with .slice(start, end): when the checker changes the values in items, middle must change with them. A list typed in by hand stays the same.
tail has to be copied out of items with .slice(start): when the checker changes the values in items, tail must change with them. A list typed in by hand stays the same.
Print middle itself, console.log(middle), with a console.log that runs. Printing items shows the same values but is not the slice; typed-in text does not count.
Print tail itself, console.log(tail), with a console.log that runs. Printing items shows the same values but is not the slice; typed-in text does not count.
Take tail from items itself, items.slice(start), not from another slice.
